Subject: GlowHealth integration: post-demo recap + dedicated sizing & next steps

Thanks again for taking the demo today, Emma — great conversation. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can align on a short integration sprint: 

Key takeaways
- Primary workloads: clinical note summarization (batch ingest), patient Q&A (low-latency chat), and an embeddings-based semantic search + reranker for historical records.
- Security constraints: VPC connectivity for Dedicated deployment, customer-managed KMS for keys, and SOC2 evidence requested by procurement.
- Target SLA: 99.9% with p95 latency targets of ~200ms for chat and ~600ms for summarize flows.

Initial technical asks (we'll validate during the sprint)
1) SDK and auth: short-lived tokens + OIDC SSO integration; we'd like to propose a client SDK bootstrap and example using our JS SDK and server-side refresh flow.
2) Routing & structured output: patient Q&A will need tool-calling (structured JSON output) for downstream systems to consume.
3) Embeddings/rerank: embeddings at 1536-d, and a reranker stage that runs top-50 -> cross-encoder rerank for precision.
4) Dedicated capacity sizing: rough requirement of sustained 200 qps chat throughput during business hours with bursts to 600 qps; concurrency and queueing model will determine VM/GPU counts.

Attachments: I've attached an initial "glowhealth-integration-checklist.xlsx" and a draft "dedicated-capacity-model-v2.csv" with throughput assumptions.

Proposed next steps (suggested owners & dates)
- Karthik: produce an integration checklist + SDK bootstrap snippet by Mon 3/12 (action: Karthik).
- Soojin: draft recommended concurrency, queue depth, and autoscale policy for Dedicated by Tue 3/13 (action: Soojin).
- Neha: coordinate procurement evidence and SOC2 artifacts; loop in procurement@glowhealth.com (action: Neha).

Can we lock a 45-minute technical deep-dive on Wed 3/14 at 10am PT? If that works I will send the invite and an agenda.

Thanks — Neha
Neha Kapoor

Thanks, Neha & Emma. I'm attaching a short technical pre-read (included in the Drive folder referenced in the spreadsheet) but calling out the high-priority items we'll want to cover in the deep-dive: 

1) SDK setup & auth-flow (high priority)
- We recommend server-side token refresh with short-lived inference tokens (TTL ~10m) and an OIDC-backed admin token for provisioning. We will provide JS and Python snippets showing the refresh flow and how to initialize the KV cache for chat.
- Attachment: sso-jwks-sample.json (example JWKS)

2) Request routing and model variants-policy
- For latency-sensitive chat: route to small-context low-latency model variants pinned on Dedicated GPUs.
- For batch summarization: route to a higher-context model on cheaper preemptible capacity during off-peak (policy-driven).

3) Structured output / tool-calling
- We'll instrument the SDK to support function/tool schemas; recommend using JSON Schema v7 for structured outputs and a single "tools" registry. Downstream systems will consume the structured payload via webhook or direct fetch. We'll demo a tool call that returns a canonical object: {"action":"create_note","note":{...}} — will include sample schemas in the pre-read.

4) Embeddings + reranker pipeline
- Embedding dimension: use 1536 float vectors quantized to FP16 for storage.
- Retrieve top-200 via ANN index (approx recall target), then lightweight transformer-based cross-encoder rerank top-50. We'll discuss estimated token compute for reranker and how that affects Dedicated capacity (shorter reranker latency = higher QPS).

5) Autoscaling, queues & concurrency model (draft numbers)
- Target steady-state: 200 QPS chat with p95 200ms => estimate requires ~3-4 low-latency workers (A100-equivalent) with per-worker concurrency tuned.
- Burst to 600 QPS: rely on burst pool + short request queuing with priority tiers (interactive traffic prioritized).
- Concurrency limits: recommend per-connection limit of 16, per-worker max inflight 512 tokens; exacts will be tuned during a capacity smoke test.

Action items (owner -> deliverable)
- Karthik: SDK bootstrap snippets + sample tool schema (deliverable in Drive) by Mon 3/12.
- Soojin: simulated capacity runbook + queue policy proposal by Tue 3/13.
- Marcus: compute cost sensitivity analysis for reranker vs approximate rerank by Tue 3/13.

I'll join the 3/14 deep-dive and bring a short bench test plan to validate the numbers.

— Karthik
